title: Developer Experience Documentation Playbook: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, and Canonical Fixes
author: Priya Nair
content:
Overview

Purpose
- This playbook defines patterns, templates, and operating procedures for all Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation: SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs-site publishing, and the canonical support-issue fixes library.
- Goal: ensure consistent, high-quality, discoverable docs that minimize support load and shorten time-to-success for developers using Redwood APIs and SDKs.

Audience
- SDK authors, technical writers, solutions engineers, developer advocates, and on-call support engineers.

Scope
- SDK guide standards (Python, JS/TS, Go, and Java)
- Quickstarts and template repos used in onboarding flows and demo apps
- API examples / reference snippets (REST + SDK)
- Docs site operating procedures (publish, review, tagging, localization triggers)
- Top support issues and canonical fixes (triage & resolution patterns)

---

1) Documentation Principles
- Write for engineers: concise examples, copy-paste code, and clear error-handling guidance.
- Prefer one task per page (e.g., "Authenticate and Generate Text with the Node SDK").
- Keep examples minimal, realistic, and production-minded (show retries, idempotency keys, and error checks).
- Maintainability: each code example must include a test or smoke-check (see Example Checklist).

2) Templates and Front Matter
Use the standard front matter for every Confluence page (first section):
- Title (short, action-oriented)
- Short description (1 sentence)
- Audience (SDK authors | App developers | Platform engineers)
- Owner (team and person)
- Status (draft | in_review | published)
- Last updated (YYYY-MM-DD)

Example page sections (required):
- Intro / What this page does
- Prereqs / Permissions / Quotas
- Quickstart (copy paste example)
- Full reference + links to SDK API docs
- Troubleshooting / Common errors
- Related pages / templates / GitHub repo

3) Quickstart & Template Guidelines
- Keep quickstarts under 10 minutes to follow (target 5–8 minutes).
- Provide both a CLI + SDK path when relevant.
- Offer a "deployable" repo template that contains: README, minimal infra (Dockerfile or Heroku/Vercel config), CI smoke test, and example requests.
- Label templates by difficulty: beginner | intermediate | advanced.

Quickstart structure (recommended):
1. Prereqs (API key, region, Node 18+/Python 3.10+, env vars)
2. Install (npm/pip)
3. Minimal example (1 file) 
4. Run & verify (curl or CLI command that returns a deterministic string)
5. Expand (add streaming, tool-calls, or embeddings)
6. Cleanup steps

4) SDK Guide Standards
- Each SDK guide must include: installation, authentication, code examples for common flows (generate/chat/embeddings/rerank), best practices, rate limiting guidance, and platform-specific caveats.
- Versioning: include the SDK version used in examples and a compatibility table mapping SDK versions to Redwood API surface versions.
- Security: demonstrate safe handling of API keys, token rotation, and recommended secrets storage.

Minimal Node (JS/TS) example to include in quickstarts:
```
// Quickstart: Generate text with Redwood JS SDK
import Redwood from '@redwood-inference/sdk';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, region: 'us-west-2' });

async function main() {
  const resp = await client.text.generate({ model: 'redwood-lg-1', prompt: 'Write a 50-word summary of Redwood Inference.' });
  console.log(resp.output[0].content);
}

main().catch(e => { console.error('Request failed:', e.message); process.exit(1); });
```

Minimal Python example:
```
# Quickstart: Generate text with Redwood Python SDK
from redwood import Redwood
client = Redwood(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'], region='us-west-2')
response = client.text.generate(model='redwood-lg-1', prompt='List three benefits of using a dedicated GPU pool.')
print(response.output[0].content)
```

5) API Examples and Reference Snippets
- Always show both REST (curl) and SDK examples for critical flows.
- Keep responses deterministic when possible (use short prompts or special test models).
- Include common header examples (Idempotency-Key, X-Request-ID) and recommended retry/backoff pseudocode.

Example curl snippet:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/text/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-lg-1","prompt":"Hello world"}'
```

6) Docs Site Operating Procedures (Publish / Review / Tags)
Publishing checklist (author):
- [ ] Content follows template and front matter is filled
- [ ] Code snippets run (smoke-tested) and include SDK version
- [ ] Security review for any secrets/examples that could leak data
- [ ] At least one reviewer sign-off
- [ ] Add labels: product-area, SDK-language, difficulty, feature
- [ ] Add related_pages links and GitHub repo link if applicable

Review flow (how-to):
1. Author creates page in draft and assigns two reviewers (one peer SDK author + one DevEx technical writer).
2. Reviewers leave inline comments and approve in Confluence.
3. Owner merges any code changes to example repo and updates package versions.
4. Page moves to in_review and then published by the owner.

Localization triggers:
- Pages with user-facing CLI/SDK wording that reach >5k monthly pageviews or are in the onboarding path are queued for localization.

Rollback and deprecation policy:
- If code examples break due to a breaking SDK change, create a deprecation note at the top of page and add a link to the canonical migration guide.
- Maintain a "deprecated examples" tag for old code samples for 12 months after deprecation.

7) Smoke Tests and CI Integration
- Every public example repository must include a `docs/smoke-test` that runs the minimal example against a test key (or local mock) as part of CI.
- If examples require network access, provide a mocked harness using recorded responses (VCR pattern) to keep CI deterministic.

8) Top Support Issues & Canonical Fixes (living list)
- Purpose: reduce repeated support cycles by documenting reproducible fixes and the triage steps. Keep this list compact and prescriptive. Update when a new issue becomes common (>= 3 repeat tickets/week).

Canonical fixes table (issue -> cause -> quick fix -> owners):
- "401 / Invalid API Key" -> "Misconfigured env var or rotated key" -> "Verify REDWOOD_API_KEY and reissue token; validate with `curl /v1/accounts/me`" -> Owner: developer-support
- "Slow first token / cold start latency" -> "Model not warmed on dedicated pool or cold container" -> "Document warmup pattern; recommend pre-warm request or use dedicated reserved pool" -> Owner: eng-serving-runtime
- "Streaming responses truncated" -> "Client timeout or intermediary (proxy) buffer" -> "Increase client read timeout; recommend chunked transfer and test behind target proxy" -> Owner: eng-developer-experience
- "Mismatched embeddings dimension" -> "Wrong model chosen for embeddings (v1 vs v2)" -> "Use compatibility table in embeddings guide and run `client.embeddings.info(model)`" -> Owner: applied-ml-and-evals
- "High 429 rate-limited errors" -> "Unbatched requests or too-high concurrency" -> "Implement exponential backoff, batching, and leaky-bucket limiter example provided" -> Owner: eng-platform

For each canonical fix include: reproduction steps, minimal failing example, and a tested fix patch with code. Store fixes in a GitHub folder: `/docs/canonical-fixes/<short-id>.md` and link from Confluence.

9) Incident/Escalation Hints for Docs Authors
- If a doc causes repeat incidents (>=5 support tickets in 7 days), open an internal incident and tag eng-sre and devex.
- Include ticket IDs and a short reproducible test case in the incident runbook.

10) Ownership and Cadence
- Document owners: each page must have an owner and secondary owner. Owners are responsible for quarterly reviews.
- Review cadence: owner performs light review every quarter and full review annually (ensure SDK versions and examples are up to date).

11) Example checklists (authors)
- Before publish:
  - Title, front matter, and 1-sentence summary present
  - Quickstart verifies in <10 minutes (yes/no)
  - Smoke test exists in example repo and passes in CI (link included)
  - At least one SDK and one curl example included
  - Troubleshooting section with top 5 errors and remediation

12) FAQs and common author Qs
- Q: How do I add a new language SDK example?
  - A: Add a minimal example under `examples/<lang>/quickstart` and link it from the page. Add the language label and update the compatibility table.
- Q: What if an example requires private customers to run?
  - A: Use a mocked example in public docs and point to the private customer-runbook in the Private Docs space (link only for authorized viewers).

13) Related templates and repos
- devex/templates/quickstart-template (GitHub)
- devex/templates/sdk-guide-template (GitHub)
- examples/public/quickstarts (repo)

14) Metrics and success criteria
- Reduction in repeat support tickets for documented issues (target: -30% YoY)
- Increase in successful self-serve signups that follow quickstart (target: +15% conversion)
- Page health: smoke tests passing in CI, <5% stale examples flagged

15) Appendix: Example canonical-fix entry (file content snippet)
Title: 401-invalid-api-key
Short description: Steps to triage and remediate invalid API key errors seen in SDKs.
Repro steps:
1. Run `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/accounts/me`
2. If 401, confirm variable set and not empty `echo $REDWOOD_API_KEY`
3. Check for newline/whitespace errors `printf "%s" "$REDWOOD_API_KEY" | od -An -t x1`
Fix: regenerate API key from Console -> API keys and update CI/Secrets manager; rotate old key and update RBAC if needed.
Owners: developer-support
